findings.issue: The data layer — cardsFor (alternate-form exclusion via id > 10000, dedupe, dex ordering), speciesIndex (type-slot assembly, generation mapping) and idFromUrl's regex — has no tests despite being the code most coupled to the API's shape.
findings.suggestion: Add vitest (`npm run qwik add vitest`) and unit-test cardsFor/speciesIndex against small fixture JSON snapshots, including the live-overlay case of one extra Pokémon and a Mega form reference.

findings.issue: Filtering, page clamping and slicing on the home page are untested: parseInt fallback, Math.min/max clamp, (page-1)*48 slice, and the three filter predicates.
findings.suggestion: Extract the filter/paginate computation into a pure function and test edge cases: page 0, NaN, page beyond total, a type value with wrong casing, and zero matches.

findings.issue: sortRows implements missing-values-last in both directions, sign-based compare with name tie-break, and aria-sort management — all client-side and untested.
findings.suggestion: Unit-test sortRows directly (it's pure) for ascending/descending on each column with null power/accuracy values, and render MovesTable with @builder.io/qwik/testing's createDOM to assert aria-sort.

findings.issue: Debounced search → URL navigation, the 'don't clobber the typing user' guard in useTask$ (app/src/routes/index.tsx:94-99), and the duplicate-nav check are untested interaction logic where regressions look like lost keystrokes or back-button desync.
findings.suggestion: Add a component test firing input events with fake timers, asserting the final URL and that navigating back updates the input.

findings.issue: The in-memory cache has untested semantics: 60s TTL including negative caching of 404s (a newly added resource stays 404 for a minute), and error-path cache eviction via value.catch.
findings.suggestion: Unit-test api() with a stubbed fetch: 404 cached, non-ok rejected, rejected promise evicted so a retry can succeed.

findings.issue: Game-select default (highest version-group order, games[games.length-1] fallback) and the ?game= validation against the games list are untested; so is the select's URL rewriting (app/src/routes/pokemon/[name]/index.tsx:216-224) which replaces history entries.
findings.suggestion: Test that an unknown ?game falls back to the highest-order group, and that switching games replaces the URL without losing other params.

findings.issue: api() throws on non-404 failures with no error boundary or test anywhere; a transient API 500 turns the page into an unhandled server error, and moveTables' Promise.all (app/src/routes/pokemon/[name]/index.tsx:60-64) rejects wholesale.
findings.suggestion: Add a Qwik City error route and a test that mocks a 500 response, asserting a friendly fallback page rather than a crash.

findings.issue: humanize, dexNumber, orDash and latestFlavorText's whitespace-collapse regex (app/src/lib/server-api.ts:60-66) are pure and used on every page, yet untested; orDash notably turns empty strings into an em dash, which a value of 0 must not trigger.
findings.suggestion: A five-line vitest file covering mr-mime, ho-oh, #0025 padding, 0 vs null vs undefined, and the \f/\n collapse would be nearly free.

findings.issue: methodRank/METHOD_ORDER plus the humanized-label localeCompare fallback implement the spec's table ordering; nothing tests that 'others alphabetically' or 'Level Up, Machine, Egg, Tutor' survive a refactor.
findings.suggestion: Unit-test the table-ordering sort with mixed known and unknown methods.

findings.issue: Not-found handling is spread across four loaders (status(404) + null checks) and a catch-all route, with the head title falling back via resolveValue; none of the 'invalid name' paths are tested by anything the app owns.
findings.suggestion: One route-level test per loader asserting null → the Not found component and a 404 status would pin the contract.

summary: The app ships zero tests of its own: no runner in devDependencies, no test script, and not a single spec file, even though Qwik's documented Vitest setup (`qwik add vitest`, @builder.io/qwik/testing createDOM) makes covering this code cheap. Everything risky — filtering, pagination, alternate-form exclusion, table sorting, URL state, caching, error paths — is guarded only by the harness's acceptance suite, which won't exist in future CI. The pure-function core in src/lib/format.ts and src/lib/server-api.ts is exactly where a few high-value unit tests would have paid for themselves.
